answer: Make each identity keep a sealed archive: 64 GB of filler encoded under its own key by a sequential sealing pass that takes a day. At random moments verifiers ask for a few byte ranges and expect them within a second, too fast to re-seal on demand, so the archive must sit on disk. Sealing is keyed per identity, so a farm can't stretch one copy across its fakes the way a painter thins one pot of pigment over many canvases. Each fake costs its own drive and day of sealing. Disk is cheap, so size should climb toward a zenith as rewards rise, keeping attacker cost on the same ridge as payoff.
